name: Shinjuku-Nishiguchi
tagline: Shinjuku in 16 minutes and Shibuya in 17 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, served by Toei Oedo Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 22 minutes to Otemachi, 16 minutes to Shinjuku, 17 minutes to Shibuya and 41 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. The station stands 33.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 10.9 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 33.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 30 m to 40.9 m, a difference of 10.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 1 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 20 clinics and 36 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is myhospital, about 5 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 都立大久保病院, about 8 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Toei Oedo Line.
congestion: Toei Oedo Line runs at 147% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 中井→東中野, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥230,000 to ¥240,000 and 2LDK ¥340,000 to ¥350,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. a small projected flood depth and plenty of places to eat out pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Shinjuku-Nishiguchi is ahead on how close the centre is and lower rent.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shinjuku-Nishiguchi. Seibu-Shinjuku has the Seibu Shinjuku Line, a different set from Shinjuku-Nishiguchi. To Toranomon, for instance, Seibu-Shinjuku takes 8 minutes longer. A one-room flat costs about ¥8,000 more at Seibu-Shinjuku.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Shinjuku; for how little of the area is in the flood projection, Shinjuku-Nishiguchi.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shinjuku-Nishiguchi. Shinjuku has 12 lines that Shinjuku-Nishiguchi does not. With more lines, Shinjuku is the better connected of the two. To Roppongi, for instance, Shinjuku is 21 minutes quicker. On how easy the shopping is, though, Shinjuku-Nishiguchi comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 11 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 5 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Toei Oedo Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
